title: Forest pond near Lake Kuchnia — multi-year field observation context
observations_reported_by_author: Periodic field inspections over multiple years indicated that the forest pond gradually lost visible water and later became dry.
During early inspections, the author suspected that a local water channel in Olszowka had become obstructed and reports manually clearing or re-cutting part of that channel.
During later field walks, the author reports finding damaged wells and concluded that the local water-management problem appeared broader than a single channel.
The author reports that the matter was submitted to the environmental-protection function of the Starostwo Powiatowe in Kwidzyn.

The author reports subsequent repair work in the wider area, including restoration of parts of a well network, restoration of ploughed-over drainage ditches and field water channels in Olszowka, and rebuilding damaged wells in the local area.
Several years later, the author reports observing more water in parts of the wider area, while the nearby forest pond did not recover in the same way.
interpretation_constraints: The field report supports the chronology of the author's observations, not a proven hydrological mechanism.
No causal link is asserted between any damaged well, ditch, channel, repair action and the drying or later water conditions.
The reported submission to the Starostwo Powiatowe in Kwidzyn and the reported repair works should be cross-checked against official records before being treated as independently verified facts.
The observed increase of water in the wider area after several years is not attributed to the repairs without hydrological, meteorological and infrastructure evidence.
The continued lack of recovery of the forest pond is an important negative observation and should be investigated separately.
recommended_official_follow_up: Obtain publicly releasable records from Starostwo Powiatowe in Kwidzyn concerning the environmental report and any documented repair works.

Compare historical and current official drainage, melioration, cadastral and water-management maps to locate wells, ditches, culverts and channels and identify documented removals, damage or restoration.
Compare the infrastructure chronology with official satellite observations, precipitation, groundwater, soil-moisture and surface-water records using matched seasons.
Treat infrastructure correlations as hypotheses until supported by independent hydrological evidence and, where appropriate, field measurements.

research_direction.goal: Develop a reproducible method for identifying where drainage wells, ditches and water channels existed, where they were removed or damaged, and whether documented infrastructure changes correlate with observed water-system changes.
research_direction.scope: Olszowka and the TEST 001 area first; later other settlements and global study areas where equivalent official/public infrastructure and Earth-observation data are legally available.
research_direction.privacy_rule: Use only lawful public/official infrastructure and environmental records; do not infer private household infrastructure or personal activity from satellite imagery.
